name: Discounted Commitments Report
description: Risk-adjusted AWS Savings Plan and Reserved Instance purchase plan: what AWS recommends, what the workload can actually sustain on its quietest hour, break-even and waste exposure per option, health blockers on existing commitments, and reconciliation against Cost Optimization Hub. Routes to the FinOps domain (cost-operations worker agent).

sections.title: AWS Discounted Commitments Report
sections.prompt:
Produce the AWS discounted commitments report.

STEP 1: Call generate_commitment_analysis with no arguments (the defaults sweep both terms, no-upfront and all-upfront, all four Savings Plan types, and all RI-eligible services over a 30-day lookback). This one call returns a field named 'report_markdown' that already contains the COMPLETE, pre-formatted report: bottom line, reconciliation against Cost Optimization Hub, existing commitment health with blockers, every recommended commitment WITH its risk rationale, eligible spend, and method.

STEP 2: Output the value of 'report_markdown' EXACTLY as returned — verbatim, in full. Do not summarize, truncate, re-order, or drop any table rows or rationale bullets. It is already correct and complete, and the section ordering is deliberate: posture blockers come BEFORE the savings number so a reader cannot skim the total without seeing that existing commitments are under-utilized.

STEP 3: After the report_markdown content, append this section only:

## Purchase sequence
- Buy nothing until every blocker listed under *Existing commitment health* is cleared — buying on top of an under-utilized commitment compounds waste.
- Buy only rows marked *Recommended*. Rows marked *Alternative* discount the same usage as a Recommended row — buy one or the other, never both. Never buy a row marked *Do not buy*.
- Among the Recommended rows, take the High-confidence ones first, in descending achievable-savings order.
- Treat Medium confidence as a smaller first tranche; re-measure after 30 days and top up rather than committing the full amount now.
- Do not buy any row whose break-even exceeds its own term — that purchase cannot pay back.
- Before buying, confirm no matching purchase is already queued (see *Commitment expiry and renewal*), so a renewal is never bought twice.

RULES: The body of the report MUST be the report_markdown field verbatim — that is what guarantees the risk-adjusted figures, the non-cancellable disclaimer, and every rationale bullet are present. Do NOT rebuild the recommendation table from the structured fields yourself. Do NOT quote the AWS best-case savings figure as if it were achievable; the achievable (risk-adjusted) figure is the headline. Do NOT add Alternative rows to any total. If 'reconciliation' reports status 'material-variance', do NOT present a single savings number as settled — the report already says why. If the tool returns 'error' instead of 'report_markdown', every Cost Explorer query failed: report the error and its 'hint' verbatim and state that no analysis was produced — this is NOT a 'no opportunity' result. If the report says no commitment opportunity was found and lists no collection warnings, that is a REAL result: report it as-is and point at the eligible-spend section, do not retry with different parameters and do not invent recommendations. If it lists collection warnings, say the result is incomplete. This tool returns LIVE data from the real AWS account (data_source='live') — do NOT add any demo/mock/sample-data disclaimer. Do NOT ask the user anything. Do NOT add follow-up questions. Execute immediately.
